title: Selection and Enrichment of Transgenic Cell Populations
author: Michael S. Fernandopulle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5fvg3n6

steps.title: Expand Transfected Cells
steps.instruction: Culture cells after transfection and expand to at least one full 6-well plate or one 10 cm dish by EDTA split. Allow approximately 1 week for post-transfection recovery and expansion.

substeps.instruction: Optionally collect genomic DNA from unpurified cells to test integration efficiency
Freeze extra heterogeneous cells as a low-passage backup

steps.title: Prepare Cells for FACS
steps.instruction: When cells reach 70% to 80% confluency (day 3 to 4 after plating), dissociate them and prepare for sorting.

substeps.instruction: Dissociate cells with Accutase
Transfer cells and Accutase solution to a conical tube
Rinse with DMEM/F12
Centrifuge for 00:05:00 at Room temperature
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor (or substitute with cold PBS with 3% BSA to reduce clumping)
Transfer cell solution to FACS tube and place on ice

steps.title: Perform FACS Sorting
steps.instruction: Perform FACS using appropriate fluorophore gating and nozzle diameter.

substeps.instruction: Sort directly onto a Matrigel-coated cell culture plate loaded with E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor
Alternatively, deposit positive cells into a separate tube, centrifuge, and replate
Alternatively, sort single cells into 96- or 384-well dishes containing E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor
Expand selected cells for clonal isolation; mark and pick positive colonies or remove negative cells

steps.title: Prepare Bead Incubation Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the buffer by supplementing PBS with 2 mM EDTA and 0.5% BSA (e.g., 47.4 ml PBS, 100 μl of 1M EDTA stock, and 2.5 ml of 10% BSA stock).

substeps.instruction: Vacuum filter the solution to degas and reduce bubbling
Store at 4 °C

steps.title: Wash and Prepare Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Prepare streptavidin-coated magnetic beads (e.g., Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend bead stock by vortexing or inversion
Pipet the required amount of bead solution into a sterile microcentrifuge tube (recommended: 10 µL per sample for positive selection; 100 µL per sample for negative selection)
Add 1 mL bead incubation buffer and invert several times to mix
Place tube on a magnetic rack, invert 2-3 times, and let rest for at least 00:01:00
Remove tube from rack
For bead volumes above 100 μl, repeat the wash process (adding buffer, magnet resting, and removing) at least twice
Resuspend beads in buffer equal to the initial volume of beads

steps.title: Dissociate and Collect Cells for Bead Selection
steps.instruction: Prepare cells for selection using EDTA split; do not use Accutase or other enzymatic reagents to avoid digesting extracellular SBP-LNGFR.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells at 37 °C for 00:10:00 to 00:15:00 until colonies begin to detach
Tilt the plate and pipet the EDTA solution 2-3 times down the well to collect cells
Transfer cells to a 15-ml conical tube (optionally filter through a cell strainer)
Wash with PBS to collect remaining cells and add to the conical tube
Count cells and calculate total number (recommended: 5 × 10^6 cells per sample; minimum 1 × 10^6 cells)
Centrifuge for 00:05:00 at Room temperature and discard supernatant
Resuspend with 1 mL buffer per sample and transfer to separate sterile 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes

steps.title: Incubate Cells with Beads
steps.instruction: Combine prepared cells and washed beads for enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Add washed beads to the cell suspension
Incubate at Room temperature for 00:30:00 on a benchtop spinner (Note: positive selection may be reduced to 10 min; negative selection may be increased to 45 min)

steps.title: Isolate and Wash Positive Fraction
steps.instruction: Separate the bead-bound cells from the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Place tube on magnet, invert 2-3 times, and let sit for at least 00:01:00
Aspirate the negative cell fraction (supernatant)
Add 1 mL buffer, remove from magnetic rack, and invert several times to resuspend beads
Repeat the aspiration and resuspension steps at least three times (or four or more if >1 × 10^7 cells were used) until the removed fraction is clear

steps.title: Release Cells from Beads
steps.instruction: Optionally release cells from the beads using biotin competition before plating.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend beads and cells with E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor and 2 mM biotin
Incubate at Room temperature for 00:30:00 on a benchtop spinner
Place on magnet for 00:01:00, invert 2-3 times, and let sit for 1 additional min
Remove supernatant with P1000

steps.title: Plate and Culture Selected Cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the purified cells to a culture vessel and maintain them.

substeps.instruction: Pipet cells and medium to a recipient culture well (if biotin levels are a concern, centrifuge and plate in fresh E8 with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor)
Return plate to 37 °C incubator and distribute cells by gently shaking the plate front-to-back and side-to-side
The following day, wash twice with PBS and add fresh E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor
Repeat the daily wash and medium change until colonies are established, then return to normal E8 conditions

steps.title: Recover Negative Fraction (Optional)
steps.instruction: If the negative fraction is required, recover the cells from the initial supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Pipet the negative fraction into a 15-ml conical tube, leaving 50-100 µL at the bottom to avoid bead carryover
Add 1 mL E8 to the tube
Centrifuge for 00:05:00 at Room temperature
Aspirate buffer and resuspend in E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor
Pipet cells and medium to a recipient culture well
Return plate to 37 °C incubator and distribute cells by gently shaking the plate
